searches.note: Twenty four searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h3, none of them the author's; four left unspent. Five were restricted to a house's own domain and read through their summaries: champagne-henriot.com three times (the Enchanteleurs 2015 page and sheets, the meaning of the name, the Hemera 2013 sheet), laurent-perrier.com (the Itération 26 pages) and louis-roederer.com (the Cristal 2015 press file and the Cristal page). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every dated change of hands, the grapes and shares, the villages, the first vintage, vintage or multi vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries; the forty five second lines were counted inside 90 to 110 words by the lint.

tested.founded: 1776 and the name of 1833: the library and the published record.
tested.story: The widow from 1932: several accounts, 1933 by the house's site, more than forty years by all. Cristal to the public in 1945: Wikipedia and Fine and Rare. Cristal 2012 the first biodynamic Cristal: The Drinks Business, Quill and Pad, Wine.com; one merchant says Cristal Rosé was biodynamic from 2007, held open. Deutz in 1993: the h2 record, refuted.
tested.cuvee: Cristal 2015: 7 grams a litre, no malolactic, 25 per cent in oak, 45 lieux dits, by the house's sheets and press file; 60 per cent Pinot Noir by the importer; six to seven years on lattes and six to twelve months after disgorging, by the house's press file, beside its general page's six years and eight months. The rhythm claimed the Tsar's wine was made only in ripe years, which no source says, and named 2016 and 2018 as sold vintages, which were not confirmed: reworded. The Vinothèque's ten years on lattes and ten after disgorging is contradicted for the 1995 (eight, six and eight by one report): the record now gives the house's whole of some twenty years.
tested.table: Read aloud: every spoken claim is the published record's or the house's.
tested.cards: The third question offered 1876 and 1974 beside 2012, years no candidate would take for biodynamic farming: replaced by 2008, 2002 and 2015, all real Cristal vintages.

changes.was: Made only in the years the house judges ripe enough, since 1876 for the Tsar and since 1945 for the public; the 2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2018 are among the vintages sold.
changes.now: Made for the Tsar's court from 1876 and sold to the public from 1945, by more than one account, in the years the house declares; the 2008, 2012, 2014 and 2015 are among the vintages sold.
changes.why: No source says the Tsar's wine was made only in ripe years; the 2016 and 2018 were not confirmed as sold.
sources: Fine and Rare: everything you need to know about Cristal Champagne

changes.was: Cristal held back by the house for about two decades, some ten years on its lattes and ten more after disgorging, before a late release.
changes.now: Cristal held back in the house's cellars for some twenty years before a late release, by the house's sheet for the 1995.
changes.why: The split is ten and ten in a pre release report and eight on lattes, six on points and eight after disgorging in a tasting report of the 1995; the house gives twenty years as a whole.
sources: Louis Roederer: Cristal Vinothèque 1995 technical sheet
A wine writer's site: Cristal Vinothèque, the quest for eternal youth
The Buyer: Cristal Vinothèque, project eternal youth
